text:
mai: quick follow-up to the retention + sampling RFC — we need to pick an actionable hot/warm/cold window and define the fallback when enrichment goes missing. ops flagged ~30% cost bump in staging when we kept full traces for 7d :grimacing:
frank: ugh. can we be more surgical? maybe keep full trace + spans for 24h, lightweight index for 7d, then compacted blobs for 90d. reduces query surface and storage. :thumbsup:
sasha: agreed on tiers, but we need a clear fallback for late enrichment. current pipeline drops billing_key if enrichment fails and we lose attribution. that was the main ops complaint.
anya: proposal: on enrichment failure, attach a sparse attribution envelope (tenant_hint, sample_bucket, fallback_cost_key) and mark trace as "partial". that keeps billing windows queryable without full enrich.
lucas: partial traces are fine, but we must ensure SLOs for critical routes — if partial attr ends up opaque for billing, customer-facing dashboards break. we need a repair job that backfills when enrichment recovers.
elaine: backfill job sounds right. small note: backfills are expensive if we do them naively. suggest backfill queue + debounce window (e.g., wait 6h for late enrichments, then run batch reconcile).
frank: +1. also add a heuristic: if trace token_count > 1k or model_call flag present, treat as high-value and keep full on hot tier for 7d. avoids losing big invoices.
mai: thanks. can someone sketch the compact schema for cold windows? short YAML snippet would help ops and storage folks.
sasha: here — compact envelope example:
```
compact_envelope:
  id: trace_id
  tenant_hint: <str>
  first_seen_ts: <iso>
  cost_bucket: <low|mid|high>
  sample_mark: <cohort-id>
  minimal_index: [span_ids]
```
nothing that ties to full spans, just enough to reference for backfill.
anya: and add field `partial: true` + `fallback_key` for failed enrichment traces. makes detection deterministic.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: patch obs-ingest config to emit `partial` envelope on enrichment timeout (job id: deploy-2026-03-17-obs).
lucas: runbook items we should add to obs playbook:
- how to detect enrichment flaps (metric: enrichment_timeout_rate > 0.5%)
- how to escalate if billing queries return >1% unknown attribution
- backfill pipeline run steps + cost estimate (per-1M traces ~ $X)
- rollback plan to revert to always-keep-full if debugging required
elaine: can we add query-time stitching support? i.e., if the compact envelope exists, we try to pull full spans from cold blob store on demand and do a lightweight rehydrate for a single call. avoids full backfill for 1-off investigations.
frank: yes, but prefer async-queued rehydrate for dashboards and a sync fast-path for debug endpoints only. rehydrate is heavy otherwise.
mai: ok action items from thread:
- finalize hot/warm/cold windows: hot=24h full, warm=7d partial+index, cold=90d compact (frank/sasha)
- enrichment fallback schema: `partial`, `fallback_key`, `minimal_index` (anya)
- backfill debounce + job design + cost estimate (elaine/lucas)
- update playbook + add detection alerts (lucas)
- implement query-time rehydrate for debug endpoints only (frank)
please ack if you own the item or want to reassign.
sasha: owning fallback schema. will drop PR with schema + example payloads today. :eyes:
anya: owning partial emit logic and tests. reassign to me and i'll coordinate with deploy.
elainE: (typo) owning backfill design, will produce cost calc and draft runbook tomorrow.
lucas: owning playbook updates + alerts. also will prototype the rehydrate queue shape.
mai: sweet. i'll add these to the RFC follow-up doc and set a 2-week milestone. link for context: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/obs-retention. any objections to the windows above?
frank: no objections. let's try to keep hot window conservative for safety.
anya: no objections. one more ask: please include a test harness that simulates late enrichment (push enrich event 12h after initial ingest) so we can validate partial->backfill flow.
mai: good call, adding test harness to the checklist.
deploy-bot: patch deployed to staging (id: d-9891). watch enrichment_timeout_rate on grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/enrichments
frank: i'll keep an eye. if we see unexpected query failures, revert.
mai: thanks all. will follow up with the milestone card and assign PR reviewers. :rocket:
